newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Bund vol steady, July option expires.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Bund vol steady, July option expires.

text.p: Implied volatility of Bund options was steady on Monday, and LIFFE brokers said there was little to move the market.
"There's no change in the volatility, and volume is too thin to get a clear idea of options prices," said one broker from a European bank.
Volatility in the new front month August serial option exercisable into the September Bund future was quoted at 5.34 percent, unchanged from Friday's levels, according to a broker from a U.S. bank.
The July serial option expired on Monday.
Volume was heavy in at-the-money strikes just ahead of expiry. At the July 101.00 strike, 1,092 contracts changed hands in both calls and puts by 1017 GMT.
In July 101.50 calls, 952 contracts traded, while turnover in puts was 385 contracts.
The September Bund future was trading at 101.15 at 1034 GMT, 17 basis points below Friday's closing price.
September volatility was quoted at 5.33 percent, flat with Friday's levels. December volatility was also steady, at 5.46 percent.
In other Bund options activity, one firm bought 500 lots of the 101.00 August call, brokers said.
The trade was for a client which was treating the options purchase like a futures position, buying the at-the-money strike for its intrinsic value, brokers added.
The futures contract responded well to the pre-market release of May German producer prices on Monday, traders said.
Producer prices rose 0.2 percent month on month, in line with expectations, and gained 1.1 percent year on year, their largest year-on-year increase since December 1995.
But the German futures and options markets lack market-moving data for the rest of the week, traders added.
